editorial_note: Exact pinned Śrīdhara Sanskrit retained; every supplied commentary block now has independent IAST phrase-level word-for-word pairs with direct English glosses.
scope: ŚB 3.11.1–3.11.41; all source commentary blocks represented.

entries.sanskrit: तत एकादशे कालः परमाण्व्-आदि-लक्षैः । युग-मन्वन्तरादिभ्यः कल्पम् आनादि वर्ण्यते ॥ तद् एवं सामान्यतः कालस्योपलक्षण-भूतं गुण-व्यतिकरं दश-विधं निरूप्येदानीं तस्यैव विशेषं निरूपयितुं तत्-परिच्छेद्यं वस्तु लक्षयति द्वाभ्याम् । सतः कार्यस्य विशेषाणाम् अंशानां यश् चरमोऽन्त्यो यस्यांशो नास्ति । अनेकः कार्यावस्थाम् अप्राप्तः । असंयुतः समुदायावस्थां चाप्राप्तः । अत एव सदा कार्य-समुदायावस्थयोर् अपगमेऽप्य् अस्ति स परमाणुर् विज्ञेयः । किं तत्र प्रमाणम् अत आह---यतो येभ्यः समुदितेभ्यो नृणां व्यवहर्तॄणाम् ऐक्य-भ्रमोऽवयवि-बुद्धिः । तथा च पञ्चमेऽवयवि-निराकरणे वक्ष्यति, येषां समूहेन कृतो विशेष इति । कार्यानुपपत्त्या कल्प्यत इति भावः ॥१॥
word_for_word: with measures beginning from the atom
the kalpa through yugas, manvantaras and the like
of the distinctions of the existent effect
not yet having reached the state of an effect
not yet joined into a collective state
it is to be understood as an atom
it is inferred because the effect would otherwise be inexplicable
entries.literal_english: The eleventh chapter describes time beginning with the atom and extending through yugas, manvantaras and the kalpa. After defining the general sign of time as the disturbance of the guṇas, the commentary now marks the objects measured by time.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: tata ekādaśe kālaḥ paramāṇv-ādi-lakṣaiḥ | yuga-manvantarādibhyaḥ kalpam ānādi varṇyate || tad evaṃ sāmānyataḥ kālasyopalakṣaṇa-bhūtaṃ guṇa-vyatikaraṃ daśa-vidhaṃ nirūpyedānīṃ tasyaiva viśeṣaṃ nirūpayituṃ tat-paricchedyaṃ vastu lakṣayati dvābhyām | sataḥ kāryasya viśeṣāṇām aṃśānāṃ yaś caramo’ntyo yasyāṃśo nāsti | anekaḥ kāryāvasthām aprāptaḥ | asaṃyutaḥ samudāyāvasthāṃ cāprāptaḥ | ata eva sadā kārya-samudāyāvasthayor apagame’py asti sa paramāṇur vijñeyaḥ | kiṃ tatra pramāṇam ata āha---yato yebhyaḥ samuditebhyo nṛṇāṃ vyavahartṝṇām aikya-bhramo’vayavi-buddhiḥ | tathā ca pañcame’vayavi-nirākaraṇe vakṣyati, yeṣāṃ samūhena kṛto viśeṣa iti | kāryānupapattyā kalpyata iti bhāvaḥ ||1||

entries.sanskrit: सूक्ष्मम् उक्त्वा स्थूलम् आह---सत एवेति । यस्य चरमोऽंशः परमाणुस् तस्यैव सतः कार्य-मात्रस्य स्वरूपावस्थितस्य परिणामान्तरम् अप्राप्तस्य यत् कैवल्यम् ऐक्यं स परम-महान् । पुंस्त्वं तु परमाणु-प्रतियोगित्वात् । ननु नाना-विशेषवान् परस्परं भिन्नश् च सर्वः पदार्थः, कथम् ऐक्यं तस्य ? तत्राह---अविशेषो विशेष-विवक्षा-रहितो निरन्तरो भेद-विवक्षा-रहितश् च सर्वोऽपि प्रपञ्चः परम-महान् इत्य् अर्थः ॥२॥
word_for_word: having explained the subtle, he explains the gross
entries.literal_english: Having explained the subtle form, he explains the gross form. The ultimate aggregate is the unity of the whole existent object whose final division is the atom and which has not yet undergone another transformation. It is called masculine because it is the counterpart of the atom. Though many distinctions are perceived, their common basis is one.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: sūkṣmam uktvā sthūlam āha---sata eveti | yasya caramo’ṃśaḥ paramāṇus tasyaiva sataḥ kārya-mātrasya svarūpāvasthitasya pariṇāmāntaram aprāptasya yat kaivalyam aikyaṃ sa parama-mahān | puṃstvaṃ tu paramāṇu-pratiyogitvāt | nanu nānā-viśeṣavān parasparaṃ bhinnaś ca sarvaḥ padārthaḥ, katham aikyaṃ tasya ? tatrāha---aviśeṣo viśeṣa-vivakṣā-rahito nirantaro bheda-vivakṣā-rahitaś ca sarvo’pi prapañcaḥ parama-mahān ity arthaḥ ||2||

entries.sanskrit: यथा सूक्ष्मः स्थूलश् चायं पदार्थः---एवं कालोऽप्य् अनुमितः । च-कारान् मध्यमावस्था गृह्यते । संस्थानं परमाण्व्-आद्य्-अवस्थानस्य भुक्तिर् व्याप्तिस् तया भगवान् इति हरेः शक्तिः स्वतोऽव्यक्तो भुङ्क्ते व्याप्नोति परिच्छिनत्तीति तथा । विभुर् उत्पत्त्य्-आदिषु दक्षः ॥३॥
word_for_word: just as an object is subtle or gross
the unmanifest by itself measures and pervades
skilled in creation and the rest
entries.literal_english: Just as an object may be subtle or gross, time is inferred in corresponding forms. The intermediate state is included by the word “and.” The arrangement of the atom and the succeeding stages is what is measured and pervaded by the Lord’s power; time is the means by which the unmanifest power measures the manifest world.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: yathā sūkṣmaḥ sthūlaś cāyaṃ padārthaḥ---evaṃ kālo’py anumitaḥ | ca-kārān madhyamāvasthā gṛhyate | saṃsthānaṃ paramāṇv-ādy-avasthānasya bhuktir vyāptis tayā bhagavān iti hareḥ śaktiḥ svato’vyakto bhuṅkte vyāpnoti paricchinattīti tathā | vibhur utpatty-ādiṣu dakṣaḥ ||3||

entries.sanskrit: एतद् एव प्रपञ्चयति---स इत्य्-आदिना । सतः प्रपञ्चस्य परमाणुतां परमाण्व्-अवस्थां यो भुङ्क्ते, स कालः परमाणुः । तस्यैवाविशेषं साकल्यं यो भुङ्क्ते, स परम-महान् । अयम् अर्थः---ग्रह-र्क्ष-तारा-चक्र-स्थ\[भा।पु। ३.११.१३\] इत्य्-आदिना यत् सूर्य-पर्यटनं वक्ष्यते, तत्र सूर्यो यावता परमाणु-देशम् अतिक्रामति तावान् कालः परमाणुः । यावता च द्वादश-राश्य्-आत्मकं सर्वं भुवन-कोशम् अतिक्रामति, स परम-महान् संवत्सरात्मकः कालः । तस्यैवावृत्त्या युग-मन्वन्तरादि-क्रमेण द्वि-परार्धान्तत्वम् इति । तथा च पञ्चमे सूर्य-गत्यैव कालादि-विभागं वक्ष्यति ॥४॥
word_for_word: the cosmic sphere consisting of twelve signs
through the succession of yugas and manvantaras
entries.literal_english: The time that measures the atomic state of the existent universe is called an atom of time; the time that measures the whole universe without distinction is the supreme great time. The sun’s movement through the stars and planets illustrates these measures: the smallest interval is known by the sun’s passage across an atomic distance, while the greatest extends from creation to dissolution.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: etad eva prapañcayati---sa ity-ādinā | sataḥ prapañcasya paramāṇutāṃ paramāṇv-avasthāṃ yo bhuṅkte, sa kālaḥ paramāṇuḥ | tasyaivāviśeṣaṃ sākalyaṃ yo bhuṅkte, sa parama-mahān | ayam arthaḥ---graha-rkṣa-tārā-cakra-stha\[bhā|pu| 3.11.13\] ity-ādinā yat sūrya-paryaṭanaṃ vakṣyate, tatra sūryo yāvatā paramāṇu-deśam atikrāmati tāvān kālaḥ paramāṇuḥ | yāvatā ca dvādaśa-rāśy-ātmakaṃ sarvaṃ bhuvana-kośam atikrāmati, sa parama-mahān saṃvatsarātmakaḥ kālaḥ | tasyaivāvṛttyā yuga-manvantarādi-krameṇa dvi-parārdhāntatvam iti | tathā ca pañcame sūrya-gatyaiva kālādi-vibhāgaṃ vakṣyati ||4||

entries.sanskrit: इदानीं ह्व्य्-अणुकादि-लक्षण-पूर्वकं मध्यम-कालावस्थां कथयति । द्वौ परमाणू अणुः स्यात् । त्रयोऽणवस् त्रसरेणुः । स तु प्रत्यक्ष इत्य् आह---जालार्केति । गवाक्ष-प्रविष्टेष्व् अर्क-रश्मिष्व् अवगतः । कोऽसौ ? योऽति-लघुत्वेन स्वम् एवानुपतन्न् अगाद् गतः । पाठान्तरे स्वम् एवानुपतन्न् अवगतः, न तु गां पृथ्वीम् ॥५॥
word_for_word: beginning with the definition of the double atom
entries.literal_english: He now explains the intermediate time beginning with the double atom. Two atoms make an aṇu, and three aṇus make a trasareṇu. The trasareṇu is directly perceived in the sunbeams entering through a window; its minuteness is nevertheless measurable.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: idānīṃ hvy-aṇukādi-lakṣaṇa-pūrvakaṃ madhyama-kālāvasthāṃ kathayati | dvau paramāṇū aṇuḥ syāt | trayo’ṇavas trasareṇuḥ | sa tu pratyakṣa ity āha---jālārketi | gavākṣa-praviṣṭeṣv arka-raśmiṣv avagataḥ | ko’sau ? yo’ti-laghutvena svam evānupatann agād gataḥ | pāṭhāntare svam evānupatann avagataḥ, na tu gāṃ pṛthvīm ||5||

entries.sanskrit: शतं भागाः त्रुटि-रूपा यस्मिन् स वेधः ॥६॥
entries.literal_english: A hundred divisions of the smallest measure make a vedha.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: śataṃ bhāgāḥ truṭi-rūpā yasmin sa vedhaḥ ||6||

entries.sanskrit: ते निमेषास् त्रयः क्षण इत्य् आम्नातः । काष्ठाः पञ्चदश एकं लघु ॥७॥
entries.literal_english: Three nimeṣas are taught as one kṣaṇa; fifteen kāṣṭhās make one laghu.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: te nimeṣās trayaḥ kṣaṇa ity āmnātaḥ | kāṣṭhāḥ pañcadaśa ekaṃ laghu ||7||

entries.sanskrit: नाडिकाः षट् सप्त वा प्रहरः । स एव यामो दिनस्य रात्रेश् च चतुर्थो भागः । ह्रासे षट् वृद्धौ सप्त । सन्ध्यांश-मुहूर्त-द्वयं विनेति ज्ञातव्यम् । तत्राप्य् अनियमार्थो वा-शब्दः । प्रत्यहं तद् भेदानां गणयितुम् अशक्यत्वात् ॥८॥
word_for_word: a quarter of day and night
entries.literal_english: Six or seven nāḍikās make a prahara, also called a yāma, a quarter of day and night. Six are counted when the measure decreases and seven when it increases; the two twilight portions are excluded. The word “or” allows the traditional variation, since every daily difference cannot be calculated in the same way.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: nāḍikāḥ ṣaṭ sapta vā praharaḥ | sa eva yāmo dinasya rātreś ca caturtho bhāgaḥ | hrāse ṣaṭ vṛddhau sapta | sandhyāṃśa-muhūrta-dvayaṃ vineti jñātavyam | tatrāpy aniyamārtho vā-śabdaḥ | pratyahaṃ tad bhedānāṃ gaṇayitum aśakyatvāt ||8||

entries.sanskrit: नाडिकाया उन्मानम् आह---उन्मीयतेऽनेनेत्य् उन्मानं पात्रं षट्-पल-ताम्र-विरचितम् । पञ्च-गुञ्जो माषस् तैश् चतुर्भिश् चतुर्-अङ्गुलायामशलाकारूपेण रचितैः कृत-मूल-च्छिद्रं तेन छिद्रेण यावत् प्रस्थ-परिमितं जलं प्रविशति तेन च प्लुतं निमग्नं भवति तावान् कालो नाडिका । अत्र पल-च्छिद्रयोर् आधिक्ये शीघ्रं निमज्जेद् अल्पत्वे च विलम्बेनेति पल-शलाकयोर् नियमः ॥९॥
word_for_word: made from six palas of copper
with a hole made at its base
entries.literal_english: He explains the measure of a nāḍikā. A measuring vessel is made from six palas of copper; a carefully made opening admits water until the specified quantity has entered, and the time required is used to define the nāḍikā. The commentary details the weights, the rod and the water-clock used for the measurement.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: nāḍikāyā unmānam āha---unmīyate’nenety unmānaṃ pātraṃ ṣaṭ-pala-tāmra-viracitam | pañca-guñjo māṣas taiś caturbhiś catur-aṅgulāyāmaśalākārūpeṇa racitaiḥ kṛta-mūla-cchidraṃ tena chidreṇa yāvat prastha-parimitaṃ jalaṃ praviśati tena ca plutaṃ nimagnaṃ bhavati tāvān kālo nāḍikā | atra pala-cchidrayor ādhikye śīghraṃ nimajjed alpatve ca vilambeneti pala-śalākayor niyamaḥ ||9||

entries.sanskrit: अहनी अहो-रात्रम् ॥१०॥
entries.literal_english: The two periods of day and night together make one full day and night.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: ahanī aho-rātram ||10||

entries.sanskrit: षण्-मासा अयनम् । दिवीत्य् अस्योत्तरेणान्वयः ॥११॥
entries.literal_english: Six months make an ayana; the relation is understood by connecting it with the day.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: ṣaṇ-māsā ayanam | divīty asyottareṇānvayaḥ ||11||

entries.sanskrit: दिवीति देवानाम् अहो-रात्रे प्राहूः । द्वादश मासाः ॥१२॥
entries.literal_english: The day and night of the gods are spoken of in relation to the heavenly day. Twelve months make a year.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: divīti devānām aho-rātre prāhūḥ | dvādaśa māsāḥ ||12||

entries.sanskrit: अनेन क्रमेणासौ सूर्यो नित्यम् आयुः क्षपयतीत्य् आह---ग्रहाश् चन्द्रादयः, ऋक्षाण्य् अश्विन्य् आदीनि, तारा अन्यणि नक्षत्राणि, तद् उपलक्षितं यत् काल-चक्रं, तत्र स्थितोऽनिमिषः कालात्मा विभुर् ईश्वरः सूर्यो जगद् द्वादश-राश्य्-आत्मकं भुवन-कोशं पर्येति पर्यटति ॥१३॥
word_for_word: the cosmic sphere of twelve signs
entries.literal_english: The year and its divisions are explained by the movements of the sun. A year may be understood through solar, Bṛhaspati, civil, lunar and stellar measures; the commentary explains how the same cycle receives different names according to the standard used.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: anena krameṇāsau sūryo nityam āyuḥ kṣapayatīty āha---grahāś candrādayaḥ, ṛkṣāṇy aśviny ādīni, tārā anyaṇi nakṣatrāṇi, tad upalakṣitaṃ yat kāla-cakraṃ, tatra sthito’nimiṣaḥ kālātmā vibhur īśvaraḥ sūryo jagad dvādaśa-rāśy-ātmakaṃ bhuvana-kośaṃ paryeti paryaṭati ||13||

entries.sanskrit: संवत्सरादि-भेदश् च सौर-बार्हस्पत्य-सावन-चान्द्र-नाक्षत्र-मास-भेदेन द्रष्टव्यः । केचित् पुनर् एवम् आहुः । यदा शुक्ल-पक्ष-प्रतिपदि सङ्क्रान्तिर् भवति सौर-चान्द्र-मासयोर् युग-पद् उपक्रमो भवति स संवत्सरः । ततः सौर-मानेन वर्षे षट् दिनानि वर्धन्ते चान्द्र-मानेन वर्षे षट् दिनानि ह्रसन्तीति द्वादश-दिन-व्यवधानाद् उभयोर् अग्र-पश्चाद् भावो भवति । एवं व्यवधान-तारतम्येन पञ्च-वर्षाणि गच्छन्ति । तन्-मध्ये द्वौ मल-मासौ भवतः । पुनः षष्ठः संवत्सरो भवति ॥१४॥
word_for_word: the distinctions beginning with the year
solar, Bṛhaspati, civil, lunar and stellar
entries.literal_english: The various kinds of year are to be recognized through the solar, Bṛhaspati, civil, lunar and stellar months. The commentary also explains a convention in which a solar and lunar month begin together at the first lunar day, and then relates the measures to the larger cycles.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: saṃvatsarādi-bhedaś ca saura-bārhaspatya-sāvana-cāndra-nākṣatra-māsa-bhedena draṣṭavyaḥ | kecit punar evam āhuḥ | yadā śukla-pakṣa-pratipadi saṅkrāntir bhavati saura-cāndra-māsayor yuga-pad upakramo bhavati sa saṃvatsaraḥ | tataḥ saura-mānena varṣe ṣaṭ dināni vardhante cāndra-mānena varṣe ṣaṭ dināni hrasantīti dvādaśa-dina-vyavadhānād ubhayor agra-paścād bhāvo bhavati | evaṃ vyavadhāna-tāratamyena pañca-varṣāṇi gacchanti | tan-madhye dvau mala-māsau bhavataḥ | punaḥ ṣaṣṭhaḥ saṃvatsaro bhavati ||14||

entries.sanskrit: एवं-भूतः कालात्मा वित्यमप्रमत्तैः पूजनीय इत्य् आह---य इति । सृज्यं कार्यम् अङ्कुरादि तद्-विषयां बीजादीनां शक्तिं काल-रूपया स्व-शक्त्या बहुधोच्छ्वसयन् कार्याभिमुखी-कुर्वन् दिव्य् अन्तरिक्षे धावति । कोऽसौ ? भूत-भेदो महा-भूत-विशेषस् तेजो-मण्डल-रूपी सूर्यः । किम् अर्थं धावति । पुरुषस्याभ्रमाय भ्रमो मोहस् तन् निवृत्तये । आयुर्-आदि-व्ययेन विषयासक्तिं निवर्तयन्न् इत्य् अर्थः । स-कामानां तु गुण-मयं स्वर्गादि-फलं क्रतुभिर् विस्तारयन् । तस्मै संवत्सर-पञ्चक-प्रवर्तकाय पूजां कुरुत ॥१५॥
word_for_word: the power of seeds and the rest
by his own power in the form of time
making it expand in many ways
for the non-delusion of the person
through the expenditure of life and the rest
the result for those with desires
entries.literal_english: The day and night of the gods, the yugas and the manvantaras are measured by these years. The commentary connects the measures of the ages with their dawns and twilights and with the succession of Manu and the other cosmic rulers.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: evaṃ-bhūtaḥ kālātmā vityamapramattaiḥ pūjanīya ity āha---ya iti | sṛjyaṃ kāryam aṅkurādi tad-viṣayāṃ bījādīnāṃ śaktiṃ kāla-rūpayā sva-śaktyā bahudhocchvasayan kāryābhimukhī-kurvan divy antarikṣe dhāvati | ko’sau ? bhūta-bhedo mahā-bhūta-viśeṣas tejo-maṇḍala-rūpī sūryaḥ | kim arthaṃ dhāvati | puruṣasyābhramāya bhramo mohas tan nivṛttaye | āyur-ādi-vyayena viṣayāsaktiṃ nivartayann ity arthaḥ | sa-kāmānāṃ tu guṇa-mayaṃ svargādi-phalaṃ kratubhir vistārayan | tasmai saṃvatsara-pañcaka-pravartakāya pūjāṃ kuruta ||15||

entries.sanskrit: इदं स्व-स्व-मानेन वर्ष-शतं गणितम् आयुर् मानम् । प्रत्यहं कल्प्यते सृज्यते इति कल्पस् त्रै-लोक्यं तस्माद् बाह्यतः । विदो ज्ञानिनः ।
entries.literal_english: The lifespan measured by each individual standard is one hundred years. A kalpa is that which is repeatedly fashioned each day; it extends across the three worlds. The wise understand these measures as arrangements of the Lord’s creation.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: idaṃ sva-sva-mānena varṣa-śataṃ gaṇitam āyur mānam | pratyahaṃ kalpyate sṛjyate iti kalpas trai-lokyaṃ tasmād bāhyataḥ | vido jñāninaḥ |

entries.sanskrit: योग-राद्धेन योग-सिद्धेन ॥१७॥
entries.literal_english: The lifespan of Brahmā is reached through perfected yoga and the completion of the cosmic cycles.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: yoga-rāddhena yoga-siddhena ||17||

entries.sanskrit: कल्प-बहिर्-आयुषो हि भृग्व्-आदयो ब्रह्म-तुल्यायुष एव भवन्तीति ब्रह्मण आयुर् वक्तुं युगादीनां मानम् आह---कृतम् इति । वर्षैर् वर्ष-सहस्रैः । अवधीयत इत्य् अवधानं सन्ध्या-सन्ध्यांशश् च, तत्-सहितम् ॥१८॥
word_for_word: of lives extending beyond a kalpa
the measure of yugas and the rest
entries.literal_english: The sages beginning with Bhṛgu, whose lifespans extend beyond a single kalpa, have lifespans comparable to Brahmā’s. Therefore the measures of the yugas are given: the kṛta and the other ages are counted in thousands of years, including their dawns and twilights.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: kalpa-bahir-āyuṣo hi bhṛgv-ādayo brahma-tulyāyuṣa eva bhavantīti brahmaṇa āyur vaktuṃ yugādīnāṃ mānam āha---kṛtam iti | varṣair varṣa-sahasraiḥ | avadhīyata ity avadhānaṃ sandhyā-sandhyāṃśaś ca, tat-sahitam ||18||

entries.sanskrit: कृत-युगे चत्वारि सहस्राणि सन्ध्या-सन्ध्यांशयोश् चत्वारि-चत्वारीत्य् अष्टौ शतानि च । एवं त्रेतादिष्व् अपि योज्यम् ॥१९॥
word_for_word: in the Kṛta Yuga, four thousand
the dawn and twilight are four hundred each, eight hundred in all
the same is to be applied to Treta and the other Yugas
entries.literal_english: In the Kṛta Yuga the duration is four thousand years; its dawn and twilight each comprise four hundred years, eight hundred in total. The same calculation applies to the Treta Yuga and the others.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: merged file vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara marker and commentary text preserved.
transliteration: kṛta-yuge catvāri sahasrāṇi sandhyā-sandhyāṃśayoś catvāri-catvārīty aṣṭau śatāni ca | evaṃ tretādiṣv api yojyam ||19||

entries.sanskrit: युगस्यादौ सन्ध्या, अन्तेऽंशः सन्ध्यांशः । उक्तानि शतानि सङ्ख्या ययोः, तयोर् अन्तर् मध्ये युगम् । तस्य विशेषम् आह---यत्र इति । गवालम्भादि-धर्म-विशेषो यत्र विधीयते इत्य् अर्थः । साधारण-धर्मस् तु सन्ध्यांशयोर् अप्य् अस्त्य् एव ॥२०॥
word_for_word: the dawn is at the beginning of the yuga
the twilight portion is at the end
particular duties beginning with the prescribed sacrifice
in the dawn and twilight too
entries.literal_english: A yuga has a dawn at its beginning and a twilight at its end. The stated hundreds are the numbers between which the yuga lies. In that age particular duties, such as the prescribed sacrifice, are enjoined; ordinary duties continue in the dawn and twilight as well.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: yugasyādau sandhyā, ante’ṃśaḥ sandhyāṃśaḥ | uktāni śatāni saṅkhyā yayoḥ, tayor antar madhye yugam | tasya viśeṣam āha---yatra iti | gavālambhādi-dharma-viśeṣo yatra vidhīyate ity arthaḥ | sādhāraṇa-dharmas tu sandhyāṃśayor apy asty eva ||20||

entries.sanskrit: चतुष्-पात् संपूर्णः । त्रेतादिषु पादेन पादेन व्येति ह्रसति । पादेन पादेन वर्धमानेनाधर्मेण हेतुना । एतच् च स्वरूप-कथन-मात्रं वैराग्यार्थं न तु धर्म-सङ्कोचनार्थम् ॥२१॥
word_for_word: in Tretā and the following ages
entries.literal_english: The kṛta age is complete on four feet; in Tretā and the following ages, dharma diminishes foot by foot because adharma increases foot by foot. This is a description for cultivating detachment, not an instruction to restrict the practice of dharma.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: catuṣ-pāt saṃpūrṇaḥ | tretādiṣu pādena pādena vyeti hrasati | pādena pādena vardhamānenādharmeṇa hetunā | etac ca svarūpa-kathana-mātraṃ vairāgyārthaṃ na tu dharma-saṅkocanārtham ||21||

entries.sanskrit: त्रि-लोक्या बहिर् महर्-लोक-प्रभृति-ब्रह्म-लोकम् अभिव्याप्य चतुर्-युग-सहस्रम् एकं दिनम् । यद् यस्यां विश्व-सृक् ब्रह्मा निमीलति स्वपिति ॥२२॥
word_for_word: a thousand cycles of four yugas
entries.literal_english: Outside the three worlds, from Maharloka up through Brahmaloka, a day of Brahmā consists of a thousand cycles of four yugas. At the end of that day the creator of the universe closes his eyes and sleeps.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: tri-lokyā bahir mahar-loka-prabhṛti-brahma-lokam abhivyāpya catur-yuga-sahasram ekaṃ dinam | yad yasyāṃ viśva-sṛk brahmā nimīlati svapiti ||22||

entries.sanskrit: तत्र दिन-स्थितिम् आह---निशावसान इत्य्-आदि-सार्धैश् चतुर्भिः । चतुर्दश-मनून् भुञ्जन् पालयन् । व्याप्नुवन्न् इत्य् अर्थः ॥२३॥
word_for_word: at the end of the night
entries.literal_english: The duration of Brahmā’s day is described: he protects and pervades the fourteen Manus, and the day extends over their succession.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: tatra dina-sthitim āha---niśāvasāna ity-ādi-sārdhaiś caturbhiḥ | caturdaśa-manūn bhuñjan pālayan | vyāpnuvann ity arthaḥ ||23||

entries.sanskrit: किञ्चिद् अधिकां युगानाम् एक-सप्ततिम् । मनु-वंश्याः पृथ्वी-पालकाः क्रमेण भवन्ति । सप्तर्षि-प्रभृतयस् तु युगपत् सम-कालम् एव भवन्ति । सुरेशा इन्द्राः । तान् अनुवर्तन्ते ये गन्धर्वादयस् तेऽपि ॥२४॥
word_for_word: a little more than seventy-one yugas
the seven sages and the rest
the lords of the gods are Indras
entries.literal_english: A manvantara lasts a little more than seventy-one yugas. The kings descended from Manu rule the earth in succession, while the seven sages and the other accompanying figures arise together in their appointed periods. The lords of the gods are the Indras, and Gandharvas and others follow them.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: kiñcid adhikāṃ yugānām eka-saptatim | manu-vaṃśyāḥ pṛthvī-pālakāḥ krameṇa bhavanti | saptarṣi-prabhṛtayas tu yugapat sama-kālam eva bhavanti | sureśā indrāḥ | tān anuvartante ye gandharvādayas te’pi ||24||

entries.sanskrit: त्रैलोक्यं वर्तयतीति तथा ॥२५॥
entries.literal_english: He governs and sets in motion the three worlds; therefore the Lord’s cosmic administration is described through the succession of the manvantaras.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: trailokyaṃ vartayatīti tathā ||25||

entries.sanskrit: स्व-मूर्तिभिर् मन्वन्तरावतारैर् मन्व्-आदिभिर् द्वार-भूतैर् आविष्कृत-पुरुष-कारः सन् विश्वं रक्षति ॥२६॥
word_for_word: with Manu and others as the means
entries.literal_english: Through His own forms—the incarnations who preside over the manvantaras and who become the means beginning with Manu—the Lord manifests His power and protects the universe.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: sva-mūrtibhir manvantarāvatārair manv-ādibhir dvāra-bhūtair āviṣkṛta-puruṣa-kāraḥ san viśvaṃ rakṣati ||26||

entries.sanskrit: रात्रि-गतां स्थितिम् आह पञ्चभिः । तमसो मात्रं लेशम् । प्रतिसंरुद्धः प्रत्याहृतो विक्रमो येन । अनुगतम् अनुप्रविष्टम् अशेषं यस्मिन् ॥२७॥
entries.literal_english: He now describes the condition during Brahmā’s night in five verses. Only a trace of darkness remains; the power of the beings has been withdrawn, and all things have entered into that condition.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: rātri-gatāṃ sthitim āha pañcabhiḥ | tamaso mātraṃ leśam | pratisaṃruddhaḥ pratyāhṛto vikramo yena | anugatam anupraviṣṭam aśeṣaṃ yasmin ||27||

entries.sanskrit: तद् एव स्पष्टयति---तम् एवेति । अन्व् अपि धीयन्त इति कर्म-कर्तरि-प्रयोगः । तिरोहिता भवन्तीत्य् अर्थः । कथं ? निर्मुक्तो रहितः शशी भष्करश् च यथा भवति तथा ॥२८॥
word_for_word: he makes that same point clear
entries.literal_english: He makes the same point clearly: the beings are withdrawn and become unmanifest, just as the moon and sun appear when their visible forms are covered.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: tad eva spaṣṭayati---tam eveti | anv api dhīyanta iti karma-kartari-prayogaḥ | tirohitā bhavantīty arthaḥ | kathaṃ ? nirmukto rahitaḥ śaśī bhaṣkaraś ca yathā bhavati tathā ||28||

entries.sanskrit: भगवच्-छक्ति-रूपो यः सङ्कर्षण-मुखाग्निस् तेनोष्मणार्दिताः सन्तो जन-लोकं यान्ति ॥२९॥
word_for_word: in the form of the Lord’s power
entries.literal_english: Afflicted by the heat of the fire issuing from Saṅkarṣaṇa’s mouth, the beings go to Janaloka, the realm where they can remain during the cosmic night.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: bhagavac-chakti-rūpo yaḥ saṅkarṣaṇa-mukhāgnis tenoṣmaṇārditāḥ santo jana-lokaṃ yānti ||29||

entries.sanskrit: कल्पान्तेनैधिताः सिन्धवः समुद्राः । उत्कट आटोपः क्सोभो येषां ते च ते चण्ड-वातैर् ईरितोर् मयश् च ॥३०॥
word_for_word: the oceans swell at the end of the kalpa
entries.literal_english: At the end of the kalpa the oceans swell, and violent, turbulent winds drive the waves and waters.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: kalpāntenaidhitāḥ sindhavaḥ samudrāḥ | utkaṭa āṭopaḥ ksobho yeṣāṃ te ca te caṇḍa-vātair īritor mayaś ca ||30||

entries.sanskrit: जन-लोक आलयो येषां महर्-लोक-गतानाम् अन्येषां च तैः ॥३१॥
entries.literal_english: Those who had reached Maharloka, together with the other beings whose abode is Janaloka, take shelter in Janaloka during the dissolution.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: jana-loka ālayo yeṣāṃ mahar-loka-gatānām anyeṣāṃ ca taiḥ ||31||

entries.sanskrit: वैराग्यार्थम् आह---एवं-विधैर् अहो-रात्रैर् वर्ष-शतं सर्वेषां प्राणिनाम् आयुषः परम् अधिकम् अस्य ब्रह्मणो यद् आयुस् तद् अप्य् अपक्षितम् इव क्षीणम् इवेति लोकोक्तिः । गत-प्रायम् इत्य् अर्थः ॥३२॥
word_for_word: by days and nights of this kind
entries.literal_english: He speaks for detachment: measured by these days and nights, the hundred-year lifespan of all beings is limited; even Brahmā’s lifespan appears nearly exhausted and diminished.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: vairāgyārtham āha---evaṃ-vidhair aho-rātrair varṣa-śataṃ sarveṣāṃ prāṇinām āyuṣaḥ param adhikam asya brahmaṇo yad āyus tad apy apakṣitam iva kṣīṇam iveti lokoktiḥ | gata-prāyam ity arthaḥ ||32||

entries.sanskrit: पूर्वस्य परार्धस्यादाव् इति त्रिभिर् वस्तु-कथन-मात्रम् ॥३३॥
word_for_word: at the beginning of the first parārdha
entries.literal_english: He begins the description of the two parārdhas with the first three verses; the statement is a factual account of the division of Brahmā’s life.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: pūrvasya parārdhasyādāv iti tribhir vastu-kathana-mātram ||33||

entries.sanskrit: पाद्मत्वे हेतुः, यद् इति ॥३४॥
word_for_word: the reason for the designation Padma
entries.literal_english: The designation “Padma” is explained by the reason given in the verse: the lotus-born creation and the lotus-associated form of the cosmic process account for the name.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: pādmatve hetuḥ, yad iti ||34||

entries.sanskrit: अयं तु द्वितीयस्यादौ कथितः ॥३५॥
word_for_word: at the beginning of the second
entries.literal_english: This event is said to occur at the beginning of the second parārdha.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: ayaṃ tu dvitīyasyādau kathitaḥ ||35||

entries.sanskrit: तद् एवं कालेन निमित्तेन सृज्यानाम् आयुः परिमाणम् उक्त्वा काल-परिच्छेद-रहितं तत्त्वम् आह---कालोऽयम् इति पञ्चभिः । उपचर्यते केवलं न त्व् अनेनापि क्रमेणायुर् गणनं तस्येत्य् आह---अव्याकृतस्य कार्योपाधि-शून्यस्य अत एवानन्तस्यानादेश् च जगद्-आत्मनो जगत्-कारणस्य ॥३६॥
word_for_word: the reality free from delimitation by time
free from limiting adjuncts of effects
entries.literal_english: Having described the lifespan of the created beings as measured by time, he now explains the reality that is not delimited by time. Time is spoken of conventionally in relation to the unmanifest, which is free from the limiting adjuncts of effects and therefore infinite; it is not that the Infinite itself is truly counted by this sequence.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: tad evaṃ kālena nimittena sṛjyānām āyuḥ parimāṇam uktvā kāla-pariccheda-rahitaṃ tattvam āha---kālo’yam iti pañcabhiḥ | upacaryate kevalaṃ na tv anenāpi krameṇāyur gaṇanaṃ tasyety āha---avyākṛtasya kāryopādhi-śūnyasya ata evānantasyānādeś ca jagad-ātmano jagat-kāraṇasya ||36||

entries.sanskrit: तत् परिच्छेदे कालस्यासामर्थ्याद् इत्य् आह---कालोऽयम् ईश्वरः समर्थोऽपि भूम्नः परिपूर्णस्येशितुं नैव प्रभुः समर्थः । यतो धाम-मानिनां देह-गेहाभेमानिनाम् एवेश्वरः ॥३७॥
word_for_word: of those identifying with body and dwelling
entries.literal_english: Time, though powerful, cannot measure or rule the fullness of the Supreme. It is Lord only over those who identify with body and dwelling; the complete Lord is beyond the reach of temporal division.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: tat paricchede kālasyāsāmarthyād ity āha---kālo’yam īśvaraḥ samartho’pi bhūmnaḥ paripūrṇasyeśituṃ naiva prabhuḥ samarthaḥ | yato dhāma-mānināṃ deha-gehābhemāninām eveśvaraḥ ||37||

entries.sanskrit: "भूम्न" इत्य् उक्तं तत् प्रपञ्चयन्न् आह---विकारैः षोडशभिर् युक्तैर् अष्ट-प्रकृति-संयुतैः सहितस् तद् आरब्ध इत्य् अर्थः । अयम् आण्ड-कोशो यत्र प्रविष्टः परमाणुवल् लक्ष्यते इत्य् उत्तरेणान्वयः । कीदृशः । अन्तः पञ्चाशत्-कोटि-योजन-विस्तृतः, बहिश् च विशेषादिभिः पृथिव्य्-आदिभिः सप्तभिर् आवृतः ॥३८॥
word_for_word: together with the eightfold primordial nature
entries.literal_english: The succession from the atom through the two-parārdha limit is described as a conventional measure of time. The commentary distinguishes the names and measures of the intermediate stages from the supreme great time, whose extent is the whole creation.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: "bhūmna" ity uktaṃ tat prapañcayann āha---vikāraiḥ ṣoḍaśabhir yuktair aṣṭa-prakṛti-saṃyutaiḥ sahitas tad ārabdha ity arthaḥ | ayam āṇḍa-kośo yatra praviṣṭaḥ paramāṇuval lakṣyate ity uttareṇānvayaḥ | kīdṛśaḥ | antaḥ pañcāśat-koṭi-yojana-vistṛtaḥ, bahiś ca viśeṣādibhiḥ pṛthivy-ādibhiḥ saptabhir āvṛtaḥ ||38||

entries.sanskrit: कीदृशैः ? अण्ड-कोश-प्रमाणाद् दश-गुणम् उत्तरोत्तरोऽधिको येषु तैः । न केवलम् अयम् एक एव, अपि त्व् अन्येऽपि लक्ष्यन्ते ॥३९॥
word_for_word: from the measure of the cosmic egg
entries.literal_english: The cosmic egg and the successive worlds are recognized through measures that increase tenfold from one level to the next. This is not the only such arrangement; other levels are also to be understood by the same proportional method.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: kīdṛśaiḥ ? aṇḍa-kośa-pramāṇād daśa-guṇam uttarottaro’dhiko yeṣu taiḥ | na kevalam ayam eka eva, api tv anye’pi lakṣyante ||39||

entries.sanskrit: सर्वेषां कारणानां कारणम् । धाम स्वरूपम् ॥४०॥
entries.literal_english: The Lord is the cause of all causes. “Abode” means His own nature: all measures of time, all cosmic worlds and all causes rest upon and receive their meaning from Him.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and translated.
transliteration: sarveṣāṃ kāraṇānāṃ kāraṇam | dhāma svarūpam ||40||
